findings.failure_path: An inherited MCP server with an existing auto-approval setting now remains enabled where the previous wrapper disabled it. If the reviewer requests its send, write or delete tool, that operation can execute before audit_codex reports tool_boundary_violation. The read-only filesystem sandbox does not contain remote MCP side effects, and rejecting the resulting verdict cannot undo them. This widens reviewer capability despite the stated acceptance requirement.
findings.smallest_fix: Enforce a packet-only tool allowlist before execution, including plugin-provided tools, while preserving selected skill loading. Retain the event audit as an additional check.

findings.failure_path: The approval assertion runs the synthetic pass behavior, and plugin_mcp likewise emits a fabricated verdict. Neither new scenario demonstrates a completed read_packet call with read-only plus approval_policy=never. The packet also omits the unchanged audit implementation and relevant negative fixtures. Consequently, the supplied evidence cannot establish either repaired end-to-end behavior or the containment guarantees now carrying the security boundary.
findings.smallest_fix: Include a verifiable real-CLI packet-read trace under the required settings, plus the relevant audit code and negative fixtures. Add a regression combining plugin inheritance with an actual packet read and a pre-execution denial test for an auto-approved non-packet tool.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The packet-selection predicates cover presence, duplication, enablement and transport binding. Successful packet reads under the required settings remain unverified.
Leaving inherited servers enabled permits external side effects before a subsequent audit can reject their calls.
Visible packet checks remain restrictive. The omitted audit implementation and negative-path fixtures prevent verification of the claimed boundary and failure handling.
The new assertions check configuration and synthetic verdicts. The source register's RED/GREEN and real-CLI statements provide claims, not inspectable execution evidence.
No public flag, exit-code or result-schema edits are visible. The npm version fields consistently advance to 0.15.5.
The diff introduces no data migration. Code and package rollback remain straightforward, but release acceptance depends on resolving the execution-boundary finding.
Visible preflight reason codes are retained. The documented approval-error diagnostic limitation remains unresolved and does not establish a new regression.
Retrospective event auditing cannot enforce execution isolation. Inherited tool descriptions also introduce an influence path that requires no forbidden tool call.
